RosterPlayer.description:
One roster row.

`account_name` is the linked account's display name and comes only from
`private.team_roster`, the Task 5 helper built for this consumer. It is the
sole path to another account's name: `user_account` is self-only under RLS.
It is never an address.

That helper hides archived and deletion-pending rows, so `account_name` is
null for them even when an account is attached. `account_linked` reads
`player.user_id` directly and stays truthful for every row, so a screen
never calls a linked player unlinked or offers to link them again.
RosterPlayer.title: RosterPlayer

UploadCreate.description:

`size_bytes` is the exact file length, not an estimate: the part plan and
the completion size check are both derived from it. The declared MIME type
is checked for a contradiction with the extension and is otherwise a hint;
Task 11 probes the stored bytes before anything trusts them.

post.description:
Sign the coach-only playback object for fifteen minutes.

The key is derived from the video's UUID, never read from the request and
never taken from a caller-supplied value, so this endpoint cannot be
steered at another object. `docs/10-security-privacy.md` keeps this object
coach-only: no player route signs it, and the published player clips of
Task 17 are separate objects entirely.

get.description:
Signed sprite sheets plus the geometry that locates a timestamp.

The geometry is recomputed from the stored duration rather than read back
from the index object, so the API, the worker, and the browser cannot drift
apart: all three call the same pure function.

post.description:
Abandon an incomplete upload. Safe to repeat.

The video row is kept in a terminal state so the Task 22 sweeper can find
it; `docs/10-security-privacy.md` gives an abandoned upload seven days from
initiation regardless of how many resumes it saw.

Finish the upload, start the retention clock, and enqueue the work.

Three phases, because assembling a multi-gigabyte object takes storage tens
of seconds and the API pool is small: authorize and reconcile in one short
transaction, talk to storage holding no lock, then transition and enqueue in
a second short transaction that authorizes again.

Idempotent by contract. The conditional UPDATE in `complete_video` is the
only transition out of `uploading`, so it settles a completion race: the
loser updates no row and reports the winner's answer.
Short-lived PUT URLs, each naming one object, one verb, and one part.
